chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Safwan, from al-Qasim ibn al-Fudayl, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever prays the five [daily prayers], fasts the month of Ramadan, performs Hajj to the Sacred House, offers the sacrifice as we have prescribed, and follows us, Allah will accept from him just as He accepts from the angels."
ai.seo_question: What conditions must be met for Allah to accept a believer's worship as perfectly as He accepts the worship of angels?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) establishes that ritual acts like prayer, fasting, and Hajj are perfected through 'ihda' (guidance/alignment) with the Ahl al-Bayt, a core Shia concept distinguishing mere physical performance from spiritual validity. This linkage elevates the believer's worship to the level of the angels, emphasizing that the Imams serve as the necessary spiritual conduit for divine acceptance. The narration underscores the Shia theological view that obedience to the Imam is intrinsic to the completeness of obligatory worship.
